SESSIONS.learn: Units and prefixes (k, M, m, µ); converting cm→m, g→kg, min→s, kJ→J; standard form

SESSIONS.learn: Using the equations sheet: find the equation, substitute, then rearrange

SESSIONS.why: Substituting first earns method marks even if the final answer is wrong.

SESSIONS.learn: Energy stores and systems; kinetic energy; gravitational potential energy; work done
SESSIONS.task: 8 questions from PMT Energy topic questions
SESSIONS.why: Every year. Multi-step KE/GPE calculations are the grade 8–9 questions.

SESSIONS.learn: Elastic potential energy; power
SESSIONS.task: 6 calculations (square the extension; convert cm→m)
SESSIONS.why: 2025: the most common error was not squaring the extension.

SESSIONS.learn: Efficiency; wasted energy and how to reduce it; thermal conductivity
SESSIONS.task: Efficiency calculations (decimal and %) + 2 'explain' questions
SESSIONS.why: Most years. Explanations must link to useful vs wasted energy.

SESSIONS.learn: Specific heat capacity
SESSIONS.task: 4 calculations + list the steps of the SHC practical
SESSIONS.why: Every year. 2025 had a 6-mark SHC method question.

SESSIONS.learn: Variables; accuracy vs precision vs resolution; random vs systematic error; uncertainty = range ÷ 2
SESSIONS.task: Make a vocabulary card + 4 practical-skills questions
SESSIONS.why: Practical marks are lost every year. 'Human error' never scores.

SESSIONS.learn: Energy resources: renewable vs non-renewable, reliability, environmental impact
SESSIONS.task: 2 'compare' questions, giving a similarity AND a difference
SESSIONS.why: Every year (Q1 in 2024 and 2025).

SESSIONS.learn: Circuit symbols; charge and current; potential difference; resistance
SESSIONS.task: Draw 10 circuit symbols from memory + 5 calculations
SESSIONS.why: Every year.

SESSIONS.learn: Series and parallel rules for current, pd and resistance; resistance of a wire
SESSIONS.task: 5 circuit questions + explain why resistors in parallel lower total resistance
SESSIONS.why: 2025: over 80% scored zero on a series/parallel explanation.

SESSIONS.learn: I–V graphs: resistor, filament lamp, diode; LDR and thermistor
SESSIONS.task: Sketch the 3 I–V graphs from memory + 3 questions
SESSIONS.why: 2025 Q3. A diode lets current flow in one direction only.

SESSIONS.learn: Electrical power and energy transferred
SESSIONS.task: 5 multi-step calculations (convert kW→W and minutes→seconds)
SESSIONS.why: Every year. Often worth 4–6 marks.

SESSIONS.learn: Mains: ac/dc, 230 V 50 Hz, plug wires and earth; National Grid and transformers

SESSIONS.why: 2022, 2024. Touching a live wire: the answer must say 'electric shock'.

SESSIONS.learn: Density; states of matter

SESSIONS.why: 2022: 6-mark density practical question.

SESSIONS.learn: Internal energy; specific heat capacity vs specific latent heat; heating curves
SESSIONS.task: 4 calculations + label a heating curve and explain the flat parts
SESSIONS.why: 2025: only 3% full marks. During a change of state, potential energy changes, not kinetic.

SESSIONS.learn: Gas pressure and temperature; pV = constant; doing work on a gas heats it (physics only)

SESSIONS.learn: Half-life and activity; contamination vs irradiation

SESSIONS.why: Every year. 2025: the answer had to say '4 half-lives'.

SESSIONS.learn: Background radiation; medical uses; fission and fusion; chain reactions (physics only)
SESSIONS.task: Describe fission in 4 steps + define fusion using 'two light nuclei join'
SESSIONS.why: 2018, 2025. Vague wording loses marks.

SESSIONS.learn: Scalars and vectors; contact and non-contact forces; weight; resultant force; free-body diagrams

SESSIONS.task: 4 calculations + 1 'explain' question

HOW: Same days, same time, same place for every session.
A predictable routine takes the decision out of starting.
One session at a time. Press Start for 25 minutes, then take the 5-minute movement break.
A short block with a clear end is easier to start and to finish.
A second 25-minute block is optional, never expected.
Stopping on time keeps physics from feeling endless.
Press 'Mark done' and pick a confidence colour straight after.
Visible progress and a quick reward.
Sit with her for the first few minutes, or work alongside her.
Working next to someone makes it easier to get going.
Watch the video first (Cognito or Free Science Lessons) with subtitles, then do the practice task.
Short, predictable input before the questions.
Always answer questions, then check them against the mark scheme.
Recalling answers fixes them in memory, and mark schemes show the exact wording examiners want.
She can swap the order of sessions within a week, but not skip them.
Some control without losing the plan.
On a bad day, do only the practice task and stop.
Something done beats nothing done.
Practice papers are split into two halves.
1 hr 45 in one go is a lot. Build up to it later.
Ask the SENCo about exam access arrangements (extra time, rest breaks, separate room, word processor) before the February mocks.
They need to be her normal way of working, and the mocks are the place to use them.
TIPS: Convert units before you substitute: cm→m, g→kg, kJ→J, minutes→seconds, mA→A.
The most common way to lose a mark in every series.
Write the equation from the sheet, substitute the numbers, then rearrange.
Substituting first earns a method mark even if the final answer is wrong.
Show every step of working.
Answers with no working often score nothing, even when the number is close.
Use brackets on the calculator when dividing by more than one number.
2025: missing brackets around the bottom of a fraction gave wrong answers.
Don't round until the final answer, and give the significant figures asked for.
Rounding 4.76% to 5% lost the mark in 2025.
Square what is squared: v² in kinetic energy, e² in elastic energy, I² in power.
2025: not squaring the extension was the most common error.
'Explain' means give the reason AND link it to the question's context.
Most students know the fact but don't apply it.
'Compare' needs a similarity and a difference, about both things named.
2025: half of students lost marks by giving only differences.
Never write 'human error'. Name the actual error, such as parallax or reaction time.
'Human error' has never scored a mark.
Use precise words: 'virtual' not 'not real', 'directly proportional' not 'proportional', 'collisions with the walls' not 'more collisions'.
Vague words lose marks on explanations.
Cross out work you don't want marked.
If two answers are left, the examiner can mark the wrong one.
Give one answer when asked for one.
Listing several answers is penalised.
